A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LieFlow research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original symmetry-discovery experiments on synthetic point clouds and rotated ModelNet10, including quantitative comparisons, masking tests, and time-schedule analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds MI-Motion experiments, further baseline comparisons, rotational-noise tests, and rectangle and functional-symmetry experiments.

M1.justification: The core loss, Algorithms 1–3, and power time schedule remain unchanged. Section 5.3 adds a limited adaptation for functional symmetry discovery: concatenating one-hot labels with spatial coordinates and learning joint spatial and label transformations under SO(2) × SO(2) on four-dimensional point clouds.

E1.justification: v3 adds MI-Motion human skeletons whose approximate symmetry comes from the observed data distribution. It also adds labeled joint-distribution tasks, rectangles with nontrivial C2 stabilizers, and rotationally perturbed observations combined with masking. The original arrow, tetrahedron, and rotated ModelNet10 coverage remains.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates LieGAN as its sole comparison method, including its one- and four-generator variants. v3 adds SGM and Augerino to the retained ModelNet10 comparison in Table 2 while preserving LieGAN, substantially broadening the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: v3 introduces relative improvement over random sampling alongside Wasserstein-1 distance. Added evaluation protocols include orbit-based labels for Augerino, conditional partial-symmetry evaluation, and a 3 × 3 combination of masking ratios and rotational-noise magnitudes. The newly specified ground distances and LieGAN coefficient prior do not establish changes from v2's unspecified experimental choices.

E4.justification: Masking-only robustness expands to rotational and combined noise tests. New analyses examine finite stabilizers, input-specific partial symmetries, and functional symmetries (Figures 18–21 and 28). Figure 21's labels conflict with Section 5.3, limiting that analysis. Existing convergence and skewness studies remain, although the explicit ModelNet10 no-power quantitative comparison is removed while its visualization remains.

E5.justification: v2 reports point estimates without seed counts or uncertainty. v3 first reports averages and standard deviations over three random seeds across the quantitative tables, including appendix results. This substantially changes uncertainty reporting but does not establish an increase from a known earlier run count. No significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Many numerical estimates are replaced. For example, ModelNet10 LieFlow Wasserstein-1 values change from 0.113 to 0.149 ± 0.013 for Tet and from 0.156 to 0.129 ± 0.005 for Ico. New baseline, relative-improvement, motion, conditional-symmetry, and noise results are reported; the ModelNet10 no-power value 0.717 is removed. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 adds Proposition 4.1 and Appendix B's assumptions, Theorem B.4, and proof that sampled transformation supports are contained in H under ideal convergence and structural conditions. This does not prove equality with H. Appendix A also refines identifiability through trivial infinitesimal stabilizers and explains finite versus continuous stabilizers; the existing flow and posterior derivations remain.

C1.justification: The central distribution-learning formulation and last-minute convergence contribution remain. v3 broadens empirical claims to MI-Motion, additional baselines, and noisy approximate symmetries. Its conclusion also replaces v2's suggestion of improved downstream sample efficiency and generalization with future evaluation of downstream utility.

C2.justification: Beyond v2's scale and prior-parameterization limitations, v3 explains failures of global support assumptions, stabilizer ambiguities, logarithm branch and cut-locus issues, and the absence of an explicit algebraic group description. The Impact Statement now discusses incorrect inferred invariances and downstream bias. Partial-symmetry discussion emphasizes input-specific subsets rather than the earlier marginal closure demonstration.

D1.justification: The training appendix is retained as v2 Appendix C becomes v3 Appendix D, preserving architectures, optimizers, hardware, and timing details. v3 newly specifies evaluation ground distances, LieGAN's uniform coefficient prior, additional baseline configurations, and MI-Motion sampling of 500,000 skeletons with 20 joints. These are limited documentation additions.

R1.justification: v3 adds He et al. (2021), Li et al. (2024), Hu et al. (2025), and the MI-Motion reference by Peng et al. (2023), and explicitly contrasts Augerino's supervision requirements with LieFlow. Most research positioning remains unchanged; publication and bibliographic updates to existing references are not additional works.

P1.justification: v3 shortens the partial-symmetry explanation, reorders contribution bullets, rewrites the conclusion and Impact Statement, and updates affiliation and publication information. The overall section sequence and much of the method and appendix prose remain intact; the added scientific sections do not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Tables gain uncertainty and relative-improvement displays; the original combined Table 2 is split between v3 Table 2 and appendix Table 5, and Table 3 becomes a grid. Motion, rectangle, conditional, functional, and noise plots substantially expand the visual evidence. Reporting defects include Table 3's reversed row/column caption and an ablation axis changed from epochs to steps while its caption still says epochs.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation beyond v2's imposed-symmetry datasets, LieGAN-only comparisons, and unreported variability through MI-Motion, SGM/Augerino comparisons, and three-seed uncertainty. The conditional support theorem and explicit failure assumptions also clarify applicability. The theorem establishes containment rather than complete recovery, and inconsistent functional-task labels and table/axis captions weaken particular additions. These limitations do not outweigh the stronger empirical foundation and clearer boundaries.
